math_notes: All judging adds integer hundredths and compares exact integers. Formatting alone divides for display; no floating-point equality judgment.
safeStart ensures all intermediate/final paths are positive; delta2 exceeds twice delta1, so route pairs have distinct results.
Visible first screenshot independently checks: 1.3 + 1.3 + 0.5 = 3.1 L.
0.3 = 0.30 is explained in onboarding, but fmt strips all trailing zeroes during actual play; the targeted equivalence misconception is not exercised afterward.
Distractor distances are generated numeric offsets, not specifically decimal-place / carrying misconception transforms; modest math-design deduction, no incorrect arithmetic found.
strengths: Readable Korean and large mobile touch targets; clear planning versus driving state.
Deliberation is untimed; three repair chances and explanatory actual-result feedback give meaningful recovery.
The fuel arithmetic controls whether the finish barrier opens, providing a real causal representation.
The model expands from tenths addition to hundredths addition/subtraction; original cast is visible in race and win states.
Nine-stage real-input completion and independent integer model enumeration supply useful evidence beyond hooks.

must_fix.item: Racing agency and escalation remain limited
must_fix.evidence: Each attempt lasts 6.4 seconds; outside guided forks, steering only collects optional score objects. The rival cannot change the win condition. Nine cycles share the driving structure.
must_fix.resolution: Future improvement: differentiated course behavior or a meaningful racing objective while keeping calculation untimed; this is a complete arithmetic-route game, not a deep kart racer.

must_fix.item: Gameplay rendering remains much simpler than title art
must_fix.evidence: Final title has convincing felt detail, while the running scene retains simple ribbon geometry, repeated trees and a small set of roadside props. The final frame is readable but still sparse.
must_fix.resolution: Treat the user’s commercial-console aspiration as an unmet quality ambition, not an achieved benchmark.

must_fix.item: Decimal equivalence is only explained, not exercised
must_fix.evidence: The 1.9 = 1.90 onboarding example is correct, but fmt removes trailing zeroes from every actual race number.
must_fix.resolution: A future question variant could place equivalent decimal spellings into actual routes.
